records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The upsampling decision `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is consulted only inside `_get_event_stats`, but the endpoint has other consumers of the same query/columns elsewhere in the request (e.g. the top-events outer/selected-columns paths and any totals computed by the dataset) that keep using raw count(), so a single response can carry both upsampled and non-upsampled numbers depending on which internal query produced them. Users comparing the timeseries values against the top-events row totals or any other aggregate computed in the same request for the same allowlisted org see mismatched counts, and the check itself performs a cache round-trip plus an options lookup on the hot stats path per request, duplicating the eligibility decision logic that will drift when a second endpoint (issues stats, dashboards previews) adopts upsampling.

records.stripped_text: [ADVISORY] The eligibility decision is cached per (organization, hash of project_ids) but the dataset/request half of the predicate (_should_apply_sample_weight_transform) is evaluated uncached after the cache lookup, so the cached value is reused across requests that differ in dataset while the fresh path recomputes the full allowlist check each time — and a Python hash() collision between two distinct project-id tuples returns another org+project-set's cached eligibility. Two different project-id sets whose sorted tuples hash-collide share a cache entry, so one set's eligibility verdict is served for the other's query; the practical trigger is rare but the failure mode is silent wrong-count (a non-allowlisted project set gets upsampled counts, or vice versa) with no error anywhere. Also, every 60-second miss writes to the shared cache on the request hot path, adding one cache write per org+project-set per minute of traffic.
